en: His father walked north and was soon joined by another man carrying similar tools.
ko: 그의 아버지는 북쪽으로 걸어갔고, 곧 비슷한 도구를 든 다른 남자와 합류했다.

raw: Within half an hour from the first starting, they were beyond the winking lamps, and the more than winking watchmen, and were out upon a lonely road.
en: Within thirty minutes, they had walked past the street lamps and watchmen into the countryside.
ko: 30분 이내에 그들은 가로등과 야경꾼들을 지나 시골로 걸어 들어갔다.

raw: Another fisherman was picked up here--and that so silently, that if Young Jerry had been superstitious, he might have supposed the second follower of the gentle craft to have, all of a sudden, split himself into two.
en: They met up with another fisherman here. It happened so quietly that if Young Jerry had been superstitious, he might have thought the second man had suddenly split into two people.
ko: 그들은 여기서 다른 낚시꾼을 만났다. 어린 제리가 미신을 믿었다면 두 번째 남자가 갑자기 두 사람으로 갈라졌다고 생각했을 정도로 너무나 조용히 일어난 일이었다.

raw: The three went on, and Young Jerry went on, until the three stopped under a bank overhanging the road. Upon the top of the bank was a low brick wall, surmounted by an iron railing.
en: The three men walked on, with Young Jerry following, until they stopped near a brick wall with an iron railing.
ko: 어린 제리가 뒤따르는 가운데 세 남자는 철제 난간이 있는 벽돌담 근처에 멈출 때까지 계속 걸어갔다.

raw: In the shadow of bank and wall the three turned out of the road, and up a blind lane, of which the wall--there, risen to some eight or ten feet high--formed one side.
en: Hidden in the shadow of a bank and a wall, the three men left the main road and turned up a dead-end lane. The wall, which was about eight or ten feet high there, made up one side of the lane.
ko: 뚝과 담장 그림자 속에 숨어 세 남자는 큰길을 벗어나 막다른 골목으로 접어들었다. 그곳에서 높이가 약 8피트에서 10피트에 달하는 담장이 골목의 한쪽을 이루고 있었다.

raw: Crouching down in a corner, peeping up the lane, the next object that Young Jerry saw, was the form of his honoured parent, pretty well defined against a watery and clouded moon, nimbly scaling an iron gate.
en: Crouching in a corner and peeking up the lane, Young Jerry next saw the shape of his father clearly outlined against a watery, cloudy moon as he quickly climbed over an iron gate.
ko: 구석에 웅크리고 골목을 훔쳐보던 어린 제리는 철문을 재빨리 넘어가는 아버지의 형체가 물기 머금은 흐린 달빛을 배경으로 뚜렷하게 윤곽을 드러내는 것을 보았다.

raw: He was soon over, and then the second fisherman got over, and then the third.
en: He was soon over, and then the second fisherman climbed over, followed by the third.
ko: 그는 곧 넘어갔고, 이어서 두 번째 낚시꾼이 넘어갔으며, 세 번째가 뒤를 따랐다.

raw: They all dropped softly on the ground within the gate, and lay there a little--listening perhaps. Then, they moved away on their hands and knees.
en: They all dropped softly onto the ground inside the gate and lay there for a moment, maybe listening. Then, they crawled away on their hands and knees.
ko: 그들은 모두 문 안쪽 땅에 부드럽게 떨어졌고, 어쩌면 소리를 들으려는 듯 잠시 그곳에 누워 있었다. 그러고 나서 그들은 손과 무릎으로 기어갔다.

raw: It was now Young Jerry’s turn to approach the gate: which he did, holding his breath.
en: Young Jerry approached the gate, holding his breath.
ko: 어린 제리는 숨을 죽인 채 문으로 다가갔다.

raw: Crouching down again in a corner there, and looking in, he made out the three fishermen creeping through some rank grass! and all the gravestones in the churchyard--it was a large churchyard that they were in--looking on like ghosts in white, while the church tower itself looked on like the ghost of a monstrous giant.
en: Crouching down again in a corner and looking through, he saw the three fishermen creeping through thick, overgrown grass! They were in a large churchyard, where all the gravestones looked like white ghosts watching them, and the church tower itself looked like the ghost of a huge giant.
ko: 구석에 다시 웅크리고 안을 들여다보았을 때, 그는 세 명의 어부들이 무성하게 자란 두꺼운 풀숲을 기어가는 것을 보았습니다! 그들은 넓은 교회 묘지에 있었는데, 그곳의 모든 묘비들은 그들을 지켜보는 하얀 유령처럼 보였고, 교회 탑 자체는 거대한 거인의 유령처럼 보였습니다.

raw: They did not creep far, before they stopped and stood upright.
en: The gravestones looked like white ghosts, and the church tower looked like a giant monster.
ko: 묘비들은 하얀 유령 같았고, 교회 탑은 거대한 괴물 같았습니다.

raw: And then they began to fish.
en: The men stopped and stood up, and then began to dig.
ko: 남자들은 가던 길을 멈추고 일어나서 땅을 파기 시작했습니다.

raw: They fished with a spade, at first.
en: They used a spade at first.
ko: 그들은 처음에 삽을 사용했습니다.

raw: Presently the honoured parent appeared to be adjusting some instrument like a great corkscrew.
en: Then his father began using a tool like a large corkscrew.
ko: 그러고 나서 그의 아버지는 커다란 코르크 마개 뽑이 같은 도구를 사용하기 시작했습니다.

raw: Whatever tools they worked with, they worked hard, until the awful striking of the church clock so terrified Young Jerry, that he made off, with his hair as stiff as his father’s.
en: They worked hard in the dark. Suddenly, the church clock struck the hour, terrifying Young Jerry so much that he ran away, his hair standing on end.
ko: 그들은 어둠 속에서 열심히 일했습니다. 갑자기 교회 시계가 정시를 알리는 종을 쳤고, 어린 제리는 머리카락이 쭈뼛 설 정도로 너무 놀라 달아났습니다.

raw: But, his long-cherished desire to know more about these matters, not only stopped him in his running away, but lured him back again.
en: However, his deep desire to learn more about his father's business not only stopped him from running away, but actually pulled him back.
ko: 하지만 아버지의 일에 대해 더 알고 싶다는 그의 깊은 욕망은 그가 도망치는 것을 멈추게 했을 뿐만 아니라, 오히려 그를 다시 끌어당겼습니다.

raw: They were still fishing perseveringly, when he peeped in at the gate for the second time; but, now they seemed to have got a bite.
en: They were still working hard at their 'fishing' when he peeked through the gate for a second time, but now it looked like they had caught something.
ko: 그가 두 번째로 문틈으로 엿보았을 때 그들은 여전히 낚시에 열중하고 있었지만, 이제는 무언가를 잡은 것 같았습니다.

raw: There was a screwing and complaining sound down below, and their bent figures were strained, as if by a weight.
en: A twisting and groaning sound came from below, and the men's bent bodies looked tense, as if they were pulling up something heavy.
ko: 아래에서 비틀리고 삐걱거리는 소리가 났고, 구부린 남자들의 몸은 마치 무거운 것을 끌어올리는 것처럼 긴장해 보였습니다.

raw: By slow degrees the weight broke away the earth upon it, and came to the surface.
en: They strained and pulled, and slowly a coffin emerged from the earth.
ko: 그들이 힘을 주어 당기자 땅속에서 서서히 관이 나타났습니다.

raw: Young Jerry very well knew what it would be; but, when he saw it, and saw his honoured parent about to wrench it open, he was so frightened, being new to the sight, that he made off again, and never stopped until he had run a mile or more.
en: Young Jerry knew exactly what it was, but when he saw it and watched his father getting ready to pry it open, he was so terrified by the unfamiliar sight that he ran away again, not stopping until he had covered a mile or more.
ko: 어린 제리는 그것이 무엇인지 정확히 알았지만, 그것을 보고 아버지가 억지로 열려고 준비하는 것을 지켜보았을 때, 낯선 광경에 너무 겁을 먹어 다시 도망쳤고 일 마일 이상을 달릴 때까지 멈추지 않았습니다.

raw: He would not have stopped then, for anything less necessary than breath, it being a spectral sort of race that he ran, and one highly desirable to get to the end of. He had a strong idea that the coffin he had seen was running after him; and, pictured as hopping on behind him, bolt upright, upon its narrow end, always on the point of overtaking him and hopping on at his side--perhaps taking his arm--it was a pursuer to shun.
en: He wouldn't have stopped then for anything less than needing to breathe. It felt like a ghostly race that he was desperate to finish. He had a terrifying thought that the coffin he had just seen was chasing him. He pictured it hopping along behind him, standing straight up on its narrow end, always right about to catch him and hop alongside him—maybe even grabbing his arm. It was definitely something he wanted to escape.
ko: 그는 숨을 쉬어야 하는 것 말고는 어떤 이유로도 멈추지 않았을 것입니다. 그것은 그가 필사적으로 끝내고 싶었던 유령과의 경주 같았습니다. 그는 방금 본 관이 자신을 쫓아오고 있다는 끔찍한 생각에 사로잡혔습니다. 그는 좁은 끝으로 똑바로 서서 그의 뒤를 깡충깡충 뛰어다니고, 항상 그를 잡을 듯이 옆에서 뛰고, 어쩌면 그의 팔을 잡을지도 모른다고 상상했습니다. 그것은 확실히 그가 벗어나고 싶은 무언가였습니다.

raw: It was an inconsistent and ubiquitous fiend too, for, while it was making the whole night behind him dreadful, he darted out into the roadway to avoid dark alleys, fearful of its coming hopping out of them like a dropsical boy’s kite without tail and wings.
en: It was a tricky, everywhere-at-once kind of monster, too. While it made the dark night behind him terrifying, he also dodged out into the street to avoid dark alleys, afraid it would hop out of them like a swollen boy's kite without a tail or wings.
ko: 그것은 교활하고 어디에나 동시에 존재하는 종류의 괴물이기도 했습니다. 그것이 그의 뒤에 있는 어두운 밤을 끔찍하게 만드는 동안, 그는 꼬리나 날개가 없는 부풀어 오른 소년의 연처럼 그것이 튀어나올까 봐 어두운 골목을 피하기 위해 거리로 피했습니다.

raw: It hid in doorways too, rubbing its horrible shoulders against doors, and drawing them up to its ears, as if it were laughing. It got into shadows on the road, and lay cunningly on its back to trip him up.
en: It seemed to hide in doorways, too, rubbing its creepy shoulders against the doors and pulling them up to its ears as if it were laughing. It snuck into the shadows on the road and lay craftily on its back to trip him up.
ko: 출입구에도 숨어 있는 것 같았고, 소름 끼치는 어깨를 문에 비비며 마치 웃는 것처럼 귀까지 어깨를 끌어올렸습니다. 길 위에서는 그림자 속으로 숨어들었고, 그를 넘어뜨리기 위해 교활하게 등을 대고 누워있었습니다.

raw: All this time it was incessantly hopping on behind and gaining on him, so that when the boy got to his own door he had reason for being half dead. And even then it would not leave him, but followed him upstairs with a bump on every stair, scrambled into bed with him, and bumped down, dead and heavy, on his breast when he fell asleep.
en: All this time, it kept hopping behind him and catching up, so that by the time the boy reached his own door, he felt half dead with fear. And even then, it wouldn't leave him alone. It followed him upstairs with a bump on every step, scrambled into bed with him, and landed heavily on his chest when he finally fell asleep.
ko: 내내 그것은 그의 뒤에서 깡충깡충 뛰며 따라잡았고, 그 소년이 자기 집 문에 도착했을 때 그는 두려움에 반쯤 죽은 것 같은 기분이 들었습니다. 그리고 심지어 그때도 그것은 그를 내버려 두지 않았습니다. 모든 계단에서 쿵쿵거리며 그를 따라 위층으로 올라갔고, 그와 함께 침대로 기어들어가 그가 마침내 잠들었을 때 그의 가슴 위에 무겁게 내려앉았습니다.

raw: From his oppressed slumber, Young Jerry in his closet was awakened after daybreak and before sunrise, by the presence of his father in the family room.
en: Young Jerry was woken from his restless sleep in his closet after dawn, but before sunrise, when he realized his father was in the main room.
ko: 어린 제리는 동이 튼 후, 하지만 해가 뜨기 전 옷장 안에서의 불안한 잠에서 깨어났고, 그의 아버지가 안방에 있다는 것을 깨달았습니다.

raw: Something had gone wrong with him; at least, so Young Jerry inferred, from the circumstance of his holding Mrs.
en: Something had gone wrong, as his father was holding Mrs.
ko: 그의 아버지가 부인을 붙잡고 있었기 때문에 무언가 잘못되었습니다.

raw: Cruncher by the ears, and knocking the back of her head against the head-board of the bed.
en: Cruncher by her ears and hitting her head against the wooden headboard of the bed.
ko: 크런처의 귀를 잡고 침대의 나무 머리판에 그녀의 머리를 부딪치고 있었습니다.

raw: “I told you I would,” said Mr.
en: "I told you I would, and I did," Mr.
ko: 내가 그러겠다고 말했고, 난 그렇게 했소,

raw: Cruncher, “and I did.”
en: Cruncher growled.
ko: 크런처 씨가 으르렁거렸습니다.

raw: “Jerry, Jerry, Jerry!” his wife implored.
en: "Jerry, Jerry, Jerry!" his wife begged.
ko: 제리, 제리, 제리! 그의 아내가 애원했습니다.

raw: “You oppose yourself to the profit of the business,” said Jerry, “and me and my partners suffer.
en: Jerry said, "You are praying against my business and making me and my partners suffer.
ko: 제리가 말했습니다. 당신은 내 사업을 반대하며 기도하고 나와 내 동업자들을 고통스럽게 만들고 있어.

raw: You was to honour and obey; why the devil don’t you?”
en: You promised to honor and obey me; why don't you?"
ko: 당신은 나를 존경하고 복종하겠다고 약속했소. 왜 그렇게 하지 않는 거요?

raw: “I try to be a good wife, Jerry,” the poor woman protested, with tears.
en: "I try to be a good wife, Jerry," she cried.
ko: 나는 좋은 아내가 되려고 노력해요, 제리, 그녀가 울부짖었습니다.

raw: “Is it being a good wife to oppose your husband’s business? Is it honouring your husband to dishonour his business?
en: "Is it being a good wife to oppose your husband's work?
ko: 남편의 일을 반대하는 것이 좋은 아내가 되는 것이오?

raw: Is it obeying your husband to disobey him on the wital subject of his business?”
en: Is it honoring me to ruin my business?"
ko: "내 사업을 망치는 것이 나를 존경하는 거요?"

raw: “You hadn’t taken to the dreadful business then, Jerry.”
en: "You didn't do this terrible work when we married, Jerry."
ko: "우리가 결혼했을 때 당신은 이런 끔찍한 일을 하지 않았어요, 제리."

raw: “It’s enough for you,” retorted Mr.
en: "That is none of your business," Jerry retorted.
ko: "당신이 알 바 아니오," 제리가 쏘아붙였다.

raw: Cruncher, “to be the wife of a honest tradesman, and not to occupy your female mind with calculations when he took to his trade or when he didn’t.
en: Cruncher said, "to be the wife of an honest tradesman, and not to fill your womanly mind with guesses about when he does his work and when he doesn't.
ko: 크런처가 말했다. "정직한 상인의 아내로서 남편이 언제 일하고 언제 일하지 않는지에 대해 여자다운 마음을 추측으로 채우지 않는 것이오.

raw: A honouring and obeying wife would let his trade alone altogether.
en: A good wife would leave my work alone.
ko: 좋은 아내라면 내 일을 내버려 둘 거요.

raw: Call yourself a religious woman?
en: You call yourself religious?
ko: 당신이 종교적이라고?

raw: If you’re a religious woman, give me a irreligious one!
en: I'd rather have an irreligious wife!
ko: 차라리 종교가 없는 아내를 갖겠어!

raw: You have no more nat’ral sense of duty than the bed of this here Thames river has of a pile, and similarly it must be knocked into you.”
en: You have no more sense of duty than the riverbed, and I have to beat it into you."
ko: 당신은 강바닥보다도 의무감이 없으니, 내가 때려서라도 가르쳐야겠소."

raw: The altercation was conducted in a low tone of voice, and terminated in the honest tradesman’s kicking off his clay-soiled boots, and lying down at his length on the floor.
en: They argued in low voices. Finally, the messenger kicked off his muddy boots and lay down on the floor to sleep.
ko: 그들은 낮은 목소리로 다투었다. 마침내 메신저는 진흙 묻은 장화를 벗어 던지고 바닥에 누워 잠을 잤다.

raw: After taking a timid peep at him lying on his back, with his rusty hands under his head for a pillow, his son lay down too, and fell asleep again.
en: After taking a nervous peek at him lying on his back, with his rusty hands tucked under his head like a pillow, his son lay down too and fell back asleep.
ko: 아들은 녹슨 두 손을 베개처럼 머리 아래에 깐 채 등을 대고 누워 있는 그를 초조하게 훔쳐본 후, 자신도 누워 다시 잠이 들었다.

raw: There was no fish for breakfast, and not much of anything else.
en: There was no food for breakfast.
ko: 아침 식사로 먹을 음식이 없었다.

raw: Mr.
en: Mr.
ko: 미스터

raw: Cruncher was out of spirits, and out of temper, and kept an iron pot-lid by him as a projectile for the correction of Mrs. Cruncher, in case he should observe any symptoms of her saying Grace.
en: Cruncher was in a terrible mood, keeping a heavy pot lid nearby to throw at his wife if she tried to say grace.
ko: 크런처는 아내가 식전 기도를 하려 하면 던지려고 무거운 냄비 뚜껑을 가까이 둔 채 몹시 기분이 언짢아 있었다.

raw: He was brushed and washed at the usual hour, and set off with his son to pursue his ostensible calling.
en: He washed and dressed, and set off with his son for work.
ko: 그는 씻고 옷을 입은 뒤 아들과 함께 일하러 나섰다.

raw: Young Jerry, walking with the stool under his arm at his father’s side along sunny and crowded Fleet-street, was a very different Young Jerry from him of the previous night, running home through darkness and solitude from his grim pursuer.
en: Young Jerry, carrying the stool under his arm beside his father in the sunny street, felt very different from the terrified boy of the night before.
ko: 어린 제리는 화창한 거리에서 아버지 곁에서 팔에 의자를 끼고 걸으면서, 전날 밤 겁에 질렸던 소년과는 아주 다른 기분이었다.

raw: His cunning was fresh with the day, and his qualms were gone with the night--in which particulars it is not improbable that he had compeers in Fleet-street and the City of London, that fine morning.
en: His cleverness returned with the morning sun, and his worries vanished with the night. In this way, it's quite likely he wasn't the only one feeling that way in Fleet Street and the City of London that beautiful morning.
ko: 그의 영리함은 아침 햇살과 함께 돌아왔고, 그의 걱정은 밤과 함께 사라졌다. 이렇게 볼 때, 그 아름다운 아침 플리트 스트리트와 런던 시에서 그런 기분을 느낀 사람은 아마 그뿐만이 아니었을 것이다.

raw: “Father,” said Young Jerry, as they walked along: taking care to keep at arm’s length and to have the stool well between them: “what’s a Resurrection-Man?”
en: "Father," Young Jerry said as they walked, keeping his distance behind the stool, "what is a Resurrection-Man?"
ko: "아버지," 어린 제리가 의자 뒤로 거리를 유지하며 걸으면서 말했다, "부활 맨이 뭐예요?"

raw: Mr.
en: Mr.
ko: 미스터

raw: Cruncher came to a stop on the pavement before he answered, “How should I know?”
en: Cruncher stopped on the pavement. "How should I know?"
ko: 크런처는 보도에서 걸음을 멈췄다. "내가 어떻게 알겠니?"

raw: “I thought you knowed everything, father,” said the artless boy. “Hem!
en: "I thought you knew everything, father," said the boy.
